themes.theme: review: AI for mechanics of materials

works.title: Autonomous Agents Coordinating Distributed Discovery Through Emergent Artifact Exchange
works.why: ScienceClaw + Infinite itself: plannerless agents, immutable artifacts with DAG lineage and provenance; the infrastructure this programme runs on and must cite. One of its four investigations is a lightweight impact-resistant ceramic screen.
works.quote: an extensible registry of over 300 interoperable scientific skills, an artifact layer that preserves full computational lineage as a directed acyclic graph (DAG), and a structured platform for agent-based scientific discourse with provenance-aware governance

works.title: A category-theoretic framework from biological mechanics to engineered stimulus-response systems
works.venue: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
works.why: Title states a category-theoretic framework mapping biological mechanics to engineered stimulus-response systems: the closest match in this batch to law-constrained biomaterial design. No abstract in the record; the paper must be read before anything is quoted from it.

works.title: From Atoms to Swarms: The Categorical Spine of Multiscale Materials Modeling and Autonomous Discovery
works.why: Review that reads multiscale modelling of silk, collagen, bone and webs as structure-preserving maps and says what category theory does and does not supply; the framing citation for tracks 5 and 6.
works.quote: Its value is operational as it forces us to declare which types survive a coarse-graining step, which symmetries a learned surrogate respects, and where each diagram fails to commute

works.title: Bioinspired123D: Generative 3D Modeling System for Bioinspired Structures
works.why: Text-to-parametric-script generator for fabricable bioinspired geometries (helical, cellular, tubular) with a critic loop; a direct tool for producing printable candidate geometries.
works.quote: We curate a domain-specific dataset of over 4,000 bioinspired and geometric design scripts spanning helical, cellular, and tubular motifs with parametric variability

works.title: Nutrient Availability Regulates an Exploration-Elaboration Trade-off in Fungal Rhizomorph Networks
works.why: Measured, non-monotonic effect of nutrient level on a self-organised fungal network, with an image-based pipeline and growth model; a ready phenotype-plus-new-condition case for track 2 (fungal, not bacterial) and a living-material route for track 5.
works.quote: Moderate nutrient limitation (0.5 × standard concentration) favoured rapid and coherent exploratory growth, whereas intermediate enrichment (1.5 × ) produced the greatest eventual network extent, reaching approximately 975 mm total strand length

works.title: Revealing Diatom‐Inspired Materials Multifunctionality
works.why: Simulation, analytical models and tests on a diatom frustule, then a 3D-printable multifunctional biomimetic material; closest fabricated precedent in this batch.
works.quote: Then a novel 3D printable multifunctional biomimetic material is proposed for applications such as porous filters, heat exchangers, drug delivery systems, lightweight structures, and robotics

works.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Extracts Structure-Function Relationships from Plants for New Materials
works.why: AI-assisted pipeline from plant literature on humidity-responsive systems to a fabricated, measured pollen-based adhesive; an end-to-end precedent for proposing and making a new biomaterial.
works.quote: culminating in the fabrication of a novel pollen-based adhesive with tunable morphology and measured shear strength

works.title: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi‐Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
works.why: Method we would reuse: ontological knowledge graph + LLM tools + multi-agent hypothesis generation and critique, applied to bio-inspired materials and reported to yield a new biocomposite concept.
works.quote: (1) large-scale ontological knowledge graphs to organize and interconnect diverse scientific concepts, (2) a suite of large language models (LLMs) and data retrieval tools, and (3) multi-agent systems with in-situ learning capabilities

works.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with generative knowledge extraction, graph-based representation, and multimodal intelligent graph reasoning
works.why: Builds a knowledge graph from a corpus of biological-materials papers and uses graph reasoning and path sampling to find gaps and propose materials, including a hierarchical mycelium-based composite. Method reusable for gap-finding in track 5.
works.quote: we have transformed a dataset comprising 1000 scientific papers focused on biological materials into a comprehensive ontological knowledge graph.

works.title: Robust myco-composites: a biocomposite platform for versatile hybrid-living materials
works.why: Measured properties and a fabricated demonstration: additively manufactured mycelium composite with stated modulus and tensile strength, plus foldable containers and textiles. Directly relevant to an architecture-facing biomaterial.
works.quote: our method yields the strongest mycelium composite reported to date with a modulus of 160 MPa and tensile strength of 0.72 MPa, which represents over a 15-fold improvement over typical mycelium composites

works.title: Multicell-Fold: geometric learning in folding multicellular life
works.why: Geometric deep-learning model of folding multicellular tissue representing cells and junction networks as one graph, predicting cell rearrangements; the closest corpus method for the tissue-morphology track.
works.quote: we achieve interpretable 4-D morphological sequence alignment, and predicting cell rearrangements before they occur at single-cell resolution.

works.title: Designing architected materials for mechanical compression via simulation, deep learning, and experimentation
works.why: Reusable workflow with a fabricated demonstration: hierarchical honeycombs designed to target stiffness and compressive stress, verified on additively manufactured samples, stated as base-material agnostic.
works.quote: We thereby demonstrate an approach for architected design that is generalizable to multiple material properties and agnostic to the identity of the base material.

works.title: Modeling and design of heterogeneous hierarchical bioinspired spider web structures using deep learning and additive manufacturing
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.why: Graph-based generative design of 3D spider-web structures conditioned on geometric parameters, with printed and mechanically tested specimens; a direct template for a printed architected proof of concept.
works.quote: Several webs are manufactured using 3D printing and tested to assess mechanical properties.

works.title: A Molecular‐Scale Understanding of Misorientation Toughening in Corals and Seashells
works.why: States a quantitative single-material design rule: slight crystal misorientation raises toughness, with stated optimum angles per polymorph from simulation and supporting nanoindentation.
works.quote: aragonite, vaterite, and calcite exhibit toughness maxima when the bicrystals are misoriented by 10°, 20°, and 30°, respectively, demonstrating that slight misorientation alone can increase fracture toughness.

works.title: Generative design, manufacturing, and molecular modeling of 3D architected materials based on natural language input
works.why: Text-to-3D architected materials that were actually 3D printed (fused deposition modelling) at varying rigidity; includes a general algorithm turning any 2D image into tileable periodic architectures, directly reusable for a printed proof of concept.
works.quote: Our work features, at its core, a generally applicable algorithm that transforms any 2D image data into hierarchical fully tileable, periodic architected materials.

works.title: Generating 3D architectured nature-inspired materials and granular media using diffusion models based on language cues
works.why: Stable Diffusion used to generate nature-inspired 3D architectures (diatom/spider-web and flame/web/wood hybrids) that were additively manufactured and assessed by coarse-grained simulation; a direct precedent for a printed, nature-inspired proof of concept.
works.quote: We create physical samples using additive manufacturing and assess material properties of materials designed via a coarse-grained particle simulation approach.

works.title: Convergent, slightly misoriented crystals toughen corals and seashells
works.why: States a quantitative design rule: slight crystal misorientation (1-40 degrees measured; simulated toughness peaks at 10, 20, 30 degrees for aragonite, vaterite, calcite) toughens by crack deflection, needs one material only and no top-down architecture, and is flagged for additive manufacturing.
works.quote: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of bicrystals reveal that aragonite, vaterite, calcite, exhibit toughness peaks when they are misoriented by 10°, 20°, 30°, respectively, demonstrating that slight misorientation alone increases crack deflection and therefore fracture toughness.

works.title: Words to Matter: De novo Architected Materials Design Using Transformer Neural Networks
works.why: Text-prompt-driven (CLIP + VQGAN) architected material designs converted to 3D models, 3D printed and analysed by finite elements; a fabricated demonstration and reusable word-to-matter pipeline.
works.quote: We then use the resulting images to generate three-dimensional models that can be realized using additive manufacturing, resulting in physical samples of these text-based materials.

works.title: Probing the Role of Bone Lamellar Patterns through Collagen Microarchitecture Mapping, Numerical Modeling, and 3D‐Printing
works.why: Bone osteon fibre-orientation patterns mapped, simulated and 3D-printed then mechanically tested; states a load-specific design rule (vertical fibres for tension, twisted for compression) for stress-tuned printed composites.
works.quote: Simulation results suggest a better performance of the vertical OM (VOM) under tensile loading and of the twisted OM (TOM) under compression, confirming earlier hypotheses.

works.title: Bioinspired hierarchical composite design using machine learning: simulation, additive manufacturing, and experiment
works.why: Design loop we would reuse: a neural network proposes hierarchical composite layouts, which are then 3D printed and mechanically tested. Direct precedent for computational design-space narrowing followed by a printed proof of concept.
works.quote: A new approach to design hierarchical materials using convolutional neural networks is proposed and validated through additive manufacturing and testing.

works.title: Combining In Silico Design and Biomimetic Assembly: A New Approach for Developing High‐Performance Dynamic Responsive Bio‐Nanomaterials
works.why: In silico design followed by self-assembly of a silk nanofibril / hydroxyapatite / chitin nanofibril nacre-like composite; gradient structure plus water sensitivity gives a programmable grab-and-release actuator. Closest template in this batch for a designed, stimulus-responsive biomaterial.
works.quote: The resultant materials that consist of silk nanofibrils (SNFs), hydroxyapatite (HAP), and chitin nanofibrils (CNFs) show nacre-like structures with mechanical strength and toughness better than most natural nacre and nacre-like nanocomposites.

works.title: The mechanics and design of a lightweight three-dimensional graphene assembly
works.why: Porous 3D graphene geometry studied by simulation and by testing 3D-printed models; the abstract reports that mechanical properties fall with density faster than in polymer foams and gives critical densities below which the architecture loses its advantage. Printed demonstration plus a density-scaling result.
works.quote: We combine bottom-up computational modeling with experiments based on 3D-printed models to investigate the mechanics of porous 3D graphene materials, resulting in new designs of carbon materials.

works.title: Hierarchically Enhanced Impact Resistance of Bioinspired Composites
works.why: 3D-printed conch-shell cross-lamellar prototype, drop-tower tested with simulation; quantifies what a second level of hierarchy buys. A stated design rule (add hierarchy to create crack-deviation paths) with a number and a printed test.
works.quote: The results show that adding the second level of cross-lamellar hierarchy can boost impact performance by 70% and 85% compared to a single-level hierarchy and the stiff constituent, respectively.

works.title: Computational Framework to Predict Failure and Performance of Bone-Inspired Materials
works.why: 2D lattice spring model that predicts performance and failure modes of previously tested 3D-printed bone-inspired composites and reproduces their toughening mechanisms. A cheap computational filter for printed designs: reusable for eliminating candidates before printing.
works.quote: In this work, we present a 2D lattice spring model to predict the performance of previously tested 3D-printed bone-inspired composites, and their failure modes.

works.title: Bone‐Inspired Materials by Design: Toughness Amplification Observed Using 3D Printing and Testing
works.why: Printed and mechanically tested bone-inspired composite; reports toughness amplification and bone-like failure modes (crack deflection, branching, bridging). Uses a multimaterial printer.
works.quote: results demonstrate that the bone‐inspired design is critical for toughness amplification and balance with material strength.

works.title: Three-Dimensional-Printing of Bio-Inspired Composites
works.why: Review of 3D printing of bio-inspired composites (bone, nacre, hair, spider silk) including stated limitations of printing; the natural entry point for the track-5 literature.
works.quote: Recent progress in additive manufacturing, especially the ability to print multiple materials at upper micrometer resolution, has given researchers an excellent instrument to design and reconstruct natural-inspired materials.

works.title: Optimization of Composite Fracture Properties: Method, Validation, and Applications
works.why: Optimisation algorithm that distributes soft and stiff phases to tune toughness, stiffness and compliance, validated against brute force; a reusable design-search method for a two-phase printed material.
works.quote: The validation shows excellent agreement between geometries obtained from the optimization algorithm and the brute force method.

works.title: Structural optimization of 3D-printed synthetic spider webs for high strength
works.why: Printed elastomeric web mimics plus modelling give an explicit design rule tying optimal material distribution to loading type; a lightweight tensile-structure result of direct interest to an architecture practice.
works.quote: We show that the loading type dictates the optimal material distribution, that is, a homogeneous distribution is better for localized loading, while stronger radial threads with weaker spiral threads is better for distributed loading.

works.title: Defect-Tolerant Bioinspired Hierarchical Composites: Simulation and Experiment
works.why: Multimaterial-printed stiff/soft hierarchical composites tested against simulation; states the rule that more hierarchy levels give more defect tolerance.
works.quote: We show that composites with more hierarchical levels dramatically improve the defect tolerance of the material.

works.title: Matriarch: A Python Library for Materials Architecture
works.why: Category-theory language for hierarchical material architecture (building blocks plus combination instructions) implemented as an open-source Python library; a direct precedent for formal, compositional design specification.
works.quote: To this end, the present paper reports a mathematical language, using category theory, to describe the architecture of a material, i.e., its set of building blocks and instructions for combining them.

works.title: Categorical prototyping: incorporating molecular mechanisms into 3D printing
works.why: Uses category theory to carry a chosen structure-mechanics relation from a nanoscale model to a macroscale multimaterial print, then validates by testing; the closest precedent in this batch for a formally constrained printed proof of concept.
works.quote: To illustrate this point, we use large-scale multi-material printing to examine the scaling of the elastic modulus of 2D carbon allotropes at the macroscale and validate our printed model using experimental testing.

works.title: 3D-printed bone-inspired composites
works.venue: Virtual Community of Pathological Anatomy (University of Castilla La Mancha)
works.why: Printed osteon-inspired polymer composite, tested in tension and with a crack in two directions; compares circular and elliptical osteon geometry at fixed volume ratio. Geometry-controls-crack-path result.
works.quote: The new material, which is a 3D-printed synthetic polymer composite, is characterized by a repeating structural unit with a circular-cylindrical shape, designed to mimic the osteons.

works.title: Modeling and additive manufacturing of bio-inspired composites with tunable fracture mechanical properties
works.why: Directly reusable: bio-inspired composites designed by mesoscale simulation, additively manufactured, tested with DIC and placed on Ashby diagrams; stiffness ratio of constituents identified as the governing design variable.
works.quote: This work enables the tailored design and manufacturing of composites assembled from inferior building blocks, that obtain optimal combinations of stiffness and toughness.

works.title: Tough Composites Inspired by Mineralized Natural Materials: Computation, 3D printing, and Testing
works.why: Directly reusable precedent: biological composite topologies (bone, sponge, nacre-like) emulated with multi-material 3D printing from brittle base materials, with model predictions agreeing with tests. Design-by-model then print-and-test is the proof-of-concept pattern for track 5.
works.quote: From base materials that are brittle and exhibit catastrophic failure, synthetic composites are created with superior fracture mechanical properties exhibiting deformation and fracture mechanisms reminiscent of mineralized biological composites.

works.title: Category Theory Based Solution for the Building Block Replacement Problem in Materials Design
works.why: Formal framework: material ologs used to define when one building block can replace another while keeping large-scale function, with a laminated composite as the worked example.
works.quote: In this paper, we apply material ologs, category‐theoretic descriptions of hierarchical materials, to rigorously define a process by which material building blocks can be replaced by others while maintaining large‐scale properties, to the extent possible.

works.title: Nanoconfinement of Spider Silk Fibrils Begets Superior Strength, Extensibility, and Toughness
works.why: States a quantitative size rule (fibril confinement diameter) that maps nanoscale properties to macroscale flaw tolerance; formalisable as a length-scale law for a hierarchical fibre material.
works.quote: We demonstrate that the geometric confinement of silk fibrils to diameters of 50 ± 30 nm is critical to facilitate a powerful mechanism by which hundreds of thousands of protein domains synergistically resist deformation and failure

works.title: Structural hierarchies define toughness and defect-tolerance despite simple and mechanically inferior brittle building blocks
works.why: Design rule: adding hierarchy levels to a single brittle base material raises defect tolerance exponentially; the clearest statement in this batch that geometry alone, in one brittle material, can buy toughness.
works.quote: Over a range of up to four hierarchy levels, we find an exponential increase in the defect-tolerance approaching hundred micrometers without introducing additional mechanisms or materials.

works.title: Category Theoretic Analysis of Hierarchical Protein Materials and Social Networks
works.why: Olog paper: category-theoretic representation of hierarchical protein material structure and function, with an explicit isomorphism to a non-material system; direct precedent for formal typed laws constraining material design.
works.quote: We show that the olog for the protein and the olog for the social network feature identical category-theoretic representations, and we proceed to precisely explicate the analogy or isomorphism between them.

works.title: Mechanics of Nano-Honeycomb Silica Structures: Size-Dependent Brittle-to-Ductile Transition
works.why: States a critical strut width below which a brittle honeycomb turns ductile; a size-dependent brittle-to-ductile law for honeycomb struts. The stated scale is in angstroms, far below any printer feature size, so transfer to a print is an open question.
works.quote: below a critical length scale around 60–80 Å, the silica struts in the nanoporous structure undergo plastic shear deformation before fracture, leading to enhanced ductility

works.title: Superductile, Wavy Silica Nanostructures Inspired by Diatom Algae
works.why: Geometric design rule with an analytical continuum model: wavy geometry (amplitude, width) gives a brittle material large extensibility by unfolding hidden length; a concept that maps onto printable geometry.
works.quote: Specifically, it is shown that for wavy silica, unfolding mechanisms are achieved for increasing amplitude and allow for greater ductility of up to 270% strain.

works.title: Cooperative deformation of hydrogen bonds in beta-strands and beta-sheet nanocrystals
works.why: Analytical elastic model predicting the optimal crystal size for maximal use of weak bonds; an explicit analytical size law, the most formalisable result in this batch.
works.quote: we predict the optimal beta-strand and beta-sheet nanocrystal size associated with reaching the maximum usage of hydrogen bonds under loading applied per unit material volume

works.title: ROBUSTNESS-STRENGTH PERFORMANCE OF HIERARCHICAL ALPHA-HELICAL PROTEIN FILAMENTS
works.why: Enumerates all hierarchical arrangements of a fixed amount of material and scores them in strength-robustness space: most are eliminated, a small fraction achieve both. Direct precedent for constraining a design space by rule and eliminating candidates.
works.quote: In contrast, for few, very specific types of combinations of the elements in hierarchies (< 2%) it is possible to maintain high strength at high robustness levels.

works.title: Geometric Confinement Governs the Rupture Strength of H-bond Assemblies at a Critical Length Scale
works.why: Explicit design rule: only 3-4 H-bonds act together, so short strands at a critical length maximise shear strength; strength comes from many small confined clusters. Directly formalisable size-effect law.
works.quote: We discover that the rupture strength of H-bond assemblies is governed by geometric confinement effects, suggesting that clusters of at most 3-4 H-bonds break concurrently, even under uniform shear loading of a much larger number of H-bonds.

works.title: Molecular nanomechanics of nascent bone: fibrillar toughening by mineralization
works.why: Measured (simulated) property set for a platelet-reinforced fibril: modulus, yield strain, fracture stress with and without mineral; and a toughening mechanism tolerating large microcracks. Quantitative target for a stiff-platelet / soft-matrix printed composite.
works.quote: mineralized collagen fibrils have a Young’s modulus of 6.23 GPa (versus 4.59 GPa for the collagen fibril), yield at a tensile strain of 6.7% (versus 5% for the collagen fibril) and feature a fracture stress of 0.6 GPa

works.title: Hierarchies, multiple energy barriers, and robustness govern the fracture mechanics of α-helical and β-sheet protein domains
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.why: Derives the hierarchical Bell model, a structure-property theory that includes hierarchy explicitly, and a robustness-at-minimal-material optimum. Strong candidate for formalisation.
works.quote: show that 3-4 parallel HBs per turn are favorable in light of the protein's mechanical and thermodynamical stability, in agreement with experimental findings that AHs feature 3.6 HBs per turn.

works.title: Nature designs tough collagen: Explaining the nanostructure of collagen fibrils
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.why: Two critical length scales and their ratio decide the failure mode of a staggered array; explains the ~300 nm molecular length. A staggered-overlap design rule directly transferable to printed staggered composites.
works.quote: The results help to explain why collagen fibers found in nature consist of TC molecules with lengths in the proximity of 300 nm

works.title: Cracking and adhesion at small scales: atomistic and continuum studies of flaw tolerant nanostructures
works.venue: Modelling and Simulation in Materials Science and Engineering
works.why: Flaw-tolerance law: below a critical feature size, Griffith fracture no longer applies and failure occurs at theoretical strength regardless of defects; size reduction is robust where shape optimisation is not. Core candidate law for constraining a printed architecture.
works.quote: An important consequence of this finding is that materials with nano-substructures may become flaw-tolerant, as the stress concentration at crack tips disappears and failure always occurs at the theoretical strength of materials, regardless of defects.

works.title: Flaw tolerant bulk and surface nanostructures of biological systems.
works.why: States design rules for a stiff-platelet / soft-matrix composite: keep the brittle phase below a critical size so flaws do not propagate, use high-aspect-ratio platelets to recover stiffness, and dissipate energy by shear in the soft phase (tension-shear chain model). Directly usable as a morphology law for a printed two-phase material, subject to the printable feature size being far above the nanoscale the paper argues from.
works.quote: We demonstrate that the nanoscale sizes allow the mineral nanoparticles in bone to achieve optimum fracture strength and the spatula nanoprotrusions in Gecko to achieve optimum adhesion strength.

works.title: GraphAgents: Knowledge Graph-Guided Agentic AI for Cross-Domain Materials Design
works.why: Knowledge-graph-guided multi-agent pipeline that proposes substitute materials under several simultaneous property constraints; method reusable for a gap-driven biomaterial search.
works.quote: Shown through the exemplar of biomedical tubing, the framework generates sustainable material alternatives to PFAS-based tubing that balance tribological performance, thermal stability, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility

works.title: Self-revising discovery systems for science: A categorical framework for agentic artificial intelligence
works.why: Title states a categorical framework for self-revising agentic discovery systems; direct formal-framework citation for track 6. No abstract in the record, so content is not confirmed beyond the title.

works.title: AutomataGPT: Transformer‐Based Forecasting and Ruleset Inference for Two‐Dimensional Cellular Automata
works.why: Infers local update rules from spatial-pattern trajectories and forecasts them; abstract names tissue morphogenesis as a target domain. Candidate method for track 2/3 rule inference.
works.quote: AutomataGPT attains 98.5% perfect one‐step forecasts and reconstructs the governing update rule with up to 96% functional (application) accuracy and 82% exact rules‐matrix match

works.title: Higher-Order Knowledge Representations for Agentic Scientific Reasoning
works.why: Hypergraph knowledge representation built from a biocomposite-scaffold corpus, with traversal used as a guardrail for hypothesis generation; directly reusable for mining this bibliography.
works.quote: our framework constructs a global hypergraph of 161,172 nodes and 320,201 hyperedges, revealing a scale-free topology (power law exponent ~1.23) organized around highly connected conceptual hubs

works.title: BeamPERL: parameter-efficient RL with verifiable rewards specializes compact LLMS for structured beam mechanics reasoning
works.why: Symbolically verified rewards on beam statics; reports that exact verification alone yields templates, not governing equations. A caution for any verifier-in-the-loop mechanics claim.
works.quote: the model generalizes compositionally (more loads, distributed loads, length scaling) but fails under topological shifts (moved supports) and applied moments that require the same equilibrium equations

works.title: Bioinspired123D: generative 3D modeling system for bioinspired structures
works.why: Journal version of Bioinspired123D (no abstract in this record); see the arXiv record for content.

works.title: Cross-domain benchmarks reveal when coordinated AI agents improve scientific inference from partial evidence
works.why: Cross-domain benchmark with frozen panels, predefined scoring, baselines and null controls, run on ScienceClaw x Infinite; states when agent coordination adds nothing. Evaluation design to reuse.
works.quote: Each case uses a frozen evaluation panel, predefined scoring protocols, explicit baselines, ablations or null controls, and stated limitations

works.title: LEIA: Learned Environment for Interactive Architected Materials
works.why: Learned surrogate for deformation and stress of architected lattices and plates, used to rank de novo designs against finite-element ground truth.
works.quote: LEIA enables efficient candidate generation and ranking for fast surrogate-guided search for de novo designs of architected materials, with stress-accurate candidate ranking validated by finite element ground truth

works.title: Models building models for discovery of graphene metamaterial design principles in the context of failure
works.why: Agent-built simulator, 96 simulations over ten architecture families; hierarchical veins redistribute load and deflect cracks. A stated design rule, at atomistic scale only.
works.quote: Selected larger hierarchical designs were about 25% stronger, with at least one-third greater work to failure, than equal-mass, equal-size controls

works.title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems for Knowledge-Grounded Material Substitution
works.why: Material substitution under manufacturing constraints using a database of lab-available materials and rejection-aware feedback; same shape as choosing within a fixed printer material list.
works.quote: The system integrates retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge-graph reasoning, a database of lab-available materials, persistent memory of intermediate results, and rejection-aware iterative feedback

works.title: In Situ Graph Reasoning and Knowledge Expansion Using Graph‐PRefLexOR
works.why: Graph-PRefLexOR: reasoning defined as a mapping from task to knowledge graph to patterns to answer, stated as inspired by category theory.
works.quote: Inspired by reinforcement learning and category theory, Graph‐PRefLexOR defines reasoning as a structured mapping from a user task to knowledge graph , patterns , and answer

works.title: Agentic deep graph reasoning yields self-organizing knowledge networks
works.venue: Journal of materials research/Pratt's guide to venture capital sources
works.why: Agentic iterative knowledge-graph expansion producing a scale-free network with bridging nodes, applied to materials design.
works.quote: the model organizes information into a scale-free network characterized by hub formation, stable modularity, and bridging nodes that link disparate knowledge clusters

works.title: Frontiers of biological material intelligence
works.why: Perspective on sensing/adaptive biological materials that names graph theory, category theory and additive manufacturing together; framing citation for the track 5 pitch.
works.quote: mathematical frameworks spanning graph theory and category theory, provide powerful tools to uncover the underlying design principles of intelligent biological materials

works.title: MultiCell: geometric learning in multicellular development
works.why: Geometric learning for multicellular development (title only; no abstract in record); likely the main track 3 method citation in this batch, to be read before use.

works.title: Sewage sludge hydrochar characterization and valorization via hydrothermal processing for 3D printing
works.why: Bio-based filler in printed composites lowers properties, but gyroid architecture recovers toughness; a measured architecture-compensates-for-material result.
works.quote: addition of hydrochar generally decreases mechanical performance of additive manufacturing composites, however, some properties such as toughness can be recovered with nature-inspired architecting into gyroid microstructures

works.title: Molecular-Scale Interactions at Mineralized Collagen Interfaces Prevent Network Percolation, Preserving Compliance
works.why: Atomistic mechanism for a compliant graded hard-soft interface: mineral-collagen bonding blocks percolation so stiffness stays below homogenization bounds. A candidate design rule for a graded printed joint.
works.quote: as mineral content increases, the tissue remains more compliant than predicted by traditional homogenization bounds.

works.title: An open-source and low-cost dual-extruder 3D printer for macroscale biotic materials
works.why: Open-source dual-extruder syringe printer for pectin/chitosan/cellulose hydrogels; a fabrication route for bio-based multi-material prints alongside a resin/SLS proof of concept.
works.quote: this printer utilizes a syringe-based mechanical extruder to deposit viscous biotic material hydrogels.

works.title: Data for "MultiCell: geometric learning in multicellular development"
works.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
works.why: Dataset record: segmented whole embryos during gastrulation; candidate available data for the tissue-morphology track (reproduce morphogenesis, test one shape prediction).
works.quote: This dataset contains four segmented Drosophila whole embryos during gastrulation.

works.title: Generative Retrieval-Augmented Ontologic Graph and Multiagent Strategies for Interpretive Large Language Model-Based Materials Design
works.why: Retrieval-augmented ontological knowledge graph strategy to curb hallucination and expose relations between concepts; directly comparable to our knowledge-graph layer.
works.quote: We show how this can be addressed using retrieval-augmented Ontological Knowledge Graph strategies.

works.title: 3D Printable Biocomposites with Tunable Environmental Degradability
works.why: Measured degradation of 3D printable pectin/chitosan/cellulose composites with composition-tunable rate; end-of-life evidence for a printed biomaterial pitch.
works.quote: demonstrated rapid degradation with up to 100% mass loss after 21 days for a pectin-based material buried in worm-laden oil.

works.title: Computational Design and Manufacturing of Sustainable Materials through First-Principles and Materiomics
works.why: Review giving a framework for sustainability in material systems and computational design of bio-based materials; anchor citation for the biomaterial gap analysis.
works.quote: We consider these through the lens of materiomics, an approach that considers material systems holistically by incorporating perspectives of all relevant scales, beginning with first-principles approaches and extending through the macroscale to consider sustainable material design from the bottom-up.

works.title: 3D Printability of Silk/Hydroxyapatite Composites for Microprosthetic Applications
works.why: Printability map relating ink rheology to print outcome for silk-hydroxyapatite composites, with mechanical comparison against pure hydroxyapatite inks.
works.quote: We demonstrate that the elastic modulus and compressive strength of parts fabricated from silk-HA inks are higher than those for rheologically comparable pure-HA inks.

works.title: Diatom-inspired architected materials using language-based deep learning: Perception, transformation and manufacturing
works.why: Language-model-generated diatom-inspired architected designs with one additively manufactured specimen reported.
works.quote: We illustrate a series of novel diatom-based designs and also report a manufactured specimen, created using additive manufacturing.

works.title: Application of the Interagency and Modeling Analysis Group Model Verification Approach for Scientific Reproducibility in a Study of Biomineralization
works.why: Worked example of independent model verification following published credibility rules, with replication of key findings; a precedent for our evaluation and verification protocol.
works.quote: Following the ten rules for credible modeling and simulation of biosciences as developed in Erdemir et al., the authors of the original paper collaborated with an external modeling group to verify the key findings of their original simulation model

works.title: STL files: Modeling and design of heterogeneous hierarchical bioinspired spider web structures using deep learning and additive manufacturing
works.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
works.why: Dataset record of STL files for the printed spider-web structures; printable geometry that could be tried directly on a resin or SLS machine.
works.quote: STL files for paper titled modeling and design of heterogeneous hierarchical bioinspired spider web structures using deep learning and additive manufacturing

works.title: Nature-inspired architected materials using unsupervised deep learning
works.why: Unsupervised GAN latent space used to generate leaf-microstructure-inspired architected materials in 2D and 3D, with a genetic algorithm optimising mechanics in latent space; a reusable generator of candidate printable architectures that a formal-law filter could then prune.
works.quote: We illustrate this end-to-end with new materials inspired by leaf microstructures, showing how biological 2D structures can be used to develop novel architected materials in 2 and 3 dimensions.

works.title: Hierarchical Multiresolution Design of Bioinspired Structural Composites Using Progressive Reinforcement Learning
works.why: Reinforcement-learning agent arranges brittle and soft phases at progressively higher resolution to cut crack-tip stress concentration, with manufactured composites agreeing with the AI optimum; a design method plus fabricated validation.
works.quote: The results show that the resulting high‐resolution designs can significantly reduce stress concentrations at crack tips and enhance mechanical resilience.

works.title: Multiscale Modeling at the Interface of Molecular Mechanics and Natural Language through Attention Neural Networks
works.why: Account framing attention networks as a "neural olog" where mathematical categorisation is learned; the clearest statement in this batch of the category-theory-for-materials line that our formal-law framework would cite.
works.quote: The transferrable power of the language-based modeling approach realizes a neural olog description, where mathematical categorization is learned by multiheaded attention, without domain knowledge in its formulation.

works.title: An automated biomateriomics platform for sustainable programmable materials discovery
works.why: Automated biomateriomics platform for sustainable programmable materials discovery (title-only record, no abstract); by title the closest precedent in this batch for an automated pipeline that discovers bio-based materials.

works.title: Rapid mechanical property prediction and de novo design of three-dimensional spider webs through graph and GraphPerceiver neural networks
works.why: Graph and GraphPerceiver models map 3D spider-web graph structure to strength and toughness, then generate de novo web architectures by multi-objective optimisation; a reusable structure-to-property method for fibre-network architectures.
works.quote: As an application of the model, we propose a computational optimization tool for synthetic web design that is used to generate synthetic, de novo spider web architectures.

works.title: Deep learning model to predict complex stress and strain fields in hierarchical composites
works.why: Conditional GAN predicting stress and strain fields directly from hierarchical composite geometry, independent of component shape and boundary conditions; a fast evaluator for candidate printed composite layouts.
works.quote: Our end-to-end deep learning model predicts physical fields like stress or strain directly from the material microstructure geometry, and reaches an astonishing accuracy not only for predicted field data but also for derivative material property predictions.

works.title: Encoding and exploring latent design space of optimal material structures via a VAE-LSTM model
works.why: VAE-LSTM learns the latent space of compliance-optimised cantilevers, generates very low density designs beyond the dataset, and shows 3D-printed prototypes; a compact structural-optimisation method with a printed demonstration.
works.quote: Ultimately, we are able to clearly visualize the space of cantilever design, generate new design with extremely low density beyond the original dataset, and obtain optimal cantilever structures inspired by nature.

works.title: In situ three-dimensional spider web construction and mechanics
works.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
works.why: Imaging and simulation of a 3D spider web during construction: geometry, strength and function are set in the first 2 days, then reinforced; explicitly pitched at fibre networks, scaffolds, 3D printing and architectural applications.
works.quote: We show that the foundation of the web geometry, strength, and functionality is created during the first 2 d of construction, after which the spider reinforces the existing network with limited expansion of the structure within the frame.

works.title: Fundamental Investigation of Biomass Interaction for Green Composites: Experiments and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
works.why: Experiments and simulation on bioadhesive-fibre green composites: near-linear tensile strength versus density, driven by hydrogen-bond content; soy protein isolate best for pinewood fibre. A measured design rule for bio-based composites.
works.quote: Experimental results reveal a good, nearly linear correlation between the composite's density and tensile strength, a finding which has rarely been reported previously.

works.title: Multiscale Modeling and Applications of Bioinspired Materials with Gyroid Structures
works.why: Book chapter on multiscale modelling and applications of bioinspired gyroid structures (title-only record); gyroids being a commonly printed lattice family is unverified background, not from the record.

works.title: Small-misorientation toughness in biominerals evolved convergently
works.why: Earlier preprint of the misorientation-toughening result: nacre, shell prisms, coral skeletons and tunicate spicules converge on small (<30 degree) misorientations of adjacent crystals, shown by simulation to toughen bicrystals.
works.quote: Here we show that diverse biominerals, including nacre and prisms from mollusk shells, coral skeletons, and tunicate spicules have different mesostructures, but they converged to similar, small (<30 degrees) misorientations of adjacent crystals at the mesoscale.

works.title: A semi-supervised approach to architected materials design using graph neural networks
works.why: Title and concepts indicate graph neural network design of truss-type architected materials; method candidate for lattice design on a printer. No abstract in record, so content not confirmed.

works.title: Multiscale structural insights of load bearing bamboo: A computational modeling approach
works.venue: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials/Journal of mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
works.why: Multiscale computational model of load-bearing bamboo (concepts: buckling, finite element, node, fibre); a natural architected column relevant to an architecture pitch. No abstract in record.

works.title: Tuning Mechanical Properties in Polycrystalline Solids Using a Deep Generative Framework
works.why: Deep learning plus genetic algorithm inverse design of toughness in polycrystalline composites, validated by MD, and a mechanism (misorientation rule) extracted from the model; reusable design-then-verify pattern.
works.quote: It is found that higher crystal misorientations are preferred for high toughness, as opposed to lower overall misorientations for low‐toughness designs.

works.title: Perspectives on three-dimensional printing of self-assembling materials and structures
works.why: Perspective on 3D printing of self-assembling materials and structures (concepts: spider silk, spinning, biomimetics); directly on the printing route. No abstract in record.

works.title: Mesomechanics of a three-dimensional spider web
works.venue: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
works.why: Mesoscale mechanics of a 3D spider web, a natural lightweight fibre architecture; candidate structural template for an architecture-facing demonstrator. No abstract in record.

works.title: The hidden structure of human enamel
works.why: Measured crystal mis-orientation in enamel rods (1-30 degrees between neighbours) and MD showing that this induces crack deflection; a quantitative toughening rule transferable to a printed architecture.
works.quote: Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that the observed mis-orientations of adjacent crystals induce crack deflection.

works.title: Biological Material Interfaces as Inspiration for Mechanical and Optical Material Designs
works.why: Chemical Reviews survey of biological material interfaces and structure-property-function relations for mechanical and optical bioinspired design; source for gap analysis and design principles.
works.quote: One essential merit of hierarchical structure is that it can optimize the interfacial features of the "building blocks" at different length scales, from the molecular level to the macroscale.

works.title: Additive Manufacturing Approaches for Hydroxyapatite‐Reinforced Composites
works.why: Review of additive manufacturing routes for hydroxyapatite-reinforced composites and biocomposites; maps printable filled-matrix options and open challenges.
works.quote: Herein, applications of AM techniques to process HA‐reinforced composites and biocomposites for the production of scaffolds with biological matrices, including cellular tissues, are reviewed.

works.title: Spider dragline silk as torsional actuator driven by humidity
works.why: Measured humidity-driven torsion of spider dragline silk with a threshold humidity and a molecular origin (proline in MaSp2); a quantified stimulus-response rule for a humidity-actuated material.
works.quote: We demonstrate that spider dragline silk exhibits a humidity-induced torsional deformation of more than 300°/mm.

works.title: Artificial intelligence design algorithm for nanocomposites optimized for shear crack resistance
works.why: CNN surrogate plus genetic algorithm ('AutoComp Designer') optimizing soft/brittle material distribution for toughness, confirmed by MD; reusable search-then-verify pattern for composite layout.
works.quote: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulations of the nanocomposite designs confirm that our AI design improves the performance by effectively decreasing the stress concentration at the crack tip.

works.title: Atomic-scale hardening mechanisms apply on larger scales in ‘architected’ materials
works.why: Nature commentary: atomic-scale hardening mechanisms applied at larger scale in architected materials; direct precedent for transferring a physical law into a printable lattice. No abstract in record.

works.title: High‐Strength, Durable All‐Silk Fibroin Hydrogels with Versatile Processability toward Multifunctional Applications
works.why: Measured property plus processability: all-silk hydrogel with MPa-range modulus that can be moulded, laser cut and machined; fills a stated gap in the modulus/strain Ashby plot.
works.quote: The Young's modulus of these new BSICT-silk fibroin hydrogels can reach up to 6.5±0.2 MPa, tens to hundreds of times higher than that of conventional hydrogels (0.01-0.1 MPa).

works.title: Multiscale Mechanics of Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces of Three-Dimensional Graphene Foams
works.why: Triply periodic minimal surfaces (primitive, diamond, gyroid) compared for elasticity, strength and fracture, with power laws across lattice size. The geometry family is directly printable and the scaling-law form is the kind of constraint a formal design law could encode. Simulation only.
works.quote: Models with different lattice sizes are utilized to derive power laws, which can connect the properties along different sizes to shed light on the multiscale mechanics of TPMSs.

works.title: Imaging and analysis of a three-dimensional spider web architecture
works.venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
works.why: Method to capture a complete 3D web as a digital fibre network at micron resolution (sheet-laser slicing plus image reconstruction), intended for mechanical simulation. A natural 3D tensile architecture turned into a model: strong link to an architecture practice.
works.quote: However, only 10% of spider species are orb-web weavers, and three-dimensional (3D) webs, such as funnel, sheet or cobwebs, are much more abundant in nature.

works.title: Materials-by-design: computation, synthesis, and characterization from atoms to structures
works.why: Review of the materials-by-design paradigm: DFT, atomistic and coarse-grained MD, continuum modelling, recombinant proteins, additive manufacturing, with silk and silk-elastin case studies. Method framing for the paper.
works.quote: This paper reviews how this paradigm creates the possibility to develop materials according to specific, rational designs from the molecular to the macroscopic scale.

works.title: De novo composite design based on machine learning algorithm
works.why: Machine-learning algorithm for de novo composite design (concepts: brittleness, toughness, optimal design); companion to the printed-and-tested 2018 study at index 276. No abstract in record.

works.title: Advanced Structural Materials by Bioinspiration
works.why: Review of design motifs common to biological structural materials, manufacturing of bio-inspired composites, case studies and limits of current techniques; a ready source for the gap analysis.
works.quote: The design motifs, common to biological structural materials, are summarized

works.title: Printing nature: Unraveling the role of nacre's mineral bridges
works.venue: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials/Journal of mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
works.why: Title and concepts indicate printed nacre-like specimens used to isolate the role of mineral bridges (concepts: toughness, stiffness, volume fraction, waviness). No abstract in record, so no number can be quoted and the printing method is not confirmed from the record.

works.title: Algorithm-driven design of fracture resistant composite materials realized through additive manufacturing
works.why: Algorithm-driven design of fracture-resistant composites realised by additive manufacturing (title; concepts include 3D printing, fracture toughness). No abstract in record.

works.title: Unraveling the Molecular Requirements for Macroscopic Silk Supercontraction
works.why: Humidity-driven contraction of dragline silk traced to polar and charged residues; in silico point mutations suppress or reverse it. A moisture-actuation mechanism with a quantified stroke.
works.quote: A less known feature of some dragline silk fibers is that they shrink along the main axis by up to 50% when exposed to high humidity, a phenomenon called supercontraction.

works.title: Unusually low and density-insensitive thermal conductivity of three-dimensional gyroid graphene
works.why: Gyroid graphene simulated for thermal conductivity: very low and nearly independent of density, with a scaling law. Suggests architected gyroid geometry as a lightweight structural insulator. Simulation only.
works.quote: we find that the thermal conductivity of gyroid graphene is more than 300 times lower than that of pristine graphene, with a bulk density of only about one-third of that of graphene.

works.title: Ion Effect and Metal-Coordinated Cross-Linking for Multiscale Design of Nereis Jaw Inspired Mechanomutable Materials
works.why: Marine-worm jaw protein made into a photo-cross-linked hydrogel whose contraction is set by Zn ions and pH through metal-coordination cross-links; multiscale model agrees with experiment. Photo-crosslinking is the nearest chemistry in this batch to a resin-printable stimulus-responsive material (the record does not say it was printed).
works.quote: These metal-coordinated cross-links induce nanoscale aggregation of Nvjp-1, which is responsible for the hydrogel contraction observed in experiments and predicted by the model.

works.title: Mutable polyelectrolyte tube arrays: mesoscale modeling and lateral force microscopy
works.why: Design rule with a number: in pH-responsive polyelectrolyte tube arrays, tube spacing (geometry) amplifies the stimulus-driven change in normal and lateral resistance. Geometry as the lever for responsiveness is transferable to a printed array. Record abstract is truncated at the start.
works.quote: with increased resistances (potential mutability) up to a factor of ∼60.

works.title: Biomimetic additive manufactured polymer composites for improved impact resistance
works.why: Title states additively manufactured biomimetic polymer composites for impact resistance; a printed demonstration. No abstract in record, so no design rule can be quoted.

works.title: Nanomechanics of silk: the fundamentals of a strong, tough and versatile material
works.why: Review of silk nanomechanics that explicitly summarises scaling laws and hierarchical length scales and their translation to synthetic materials; candidate source of laws to formalise.
works.quote: We conclude the discussion with a summary of key scaling laws, an attempt model and define hierarchical length-scales, and the translation to synthetic materials.

works.title: Osmotic pressure induced tensile forces in tendon collagen
works.why: Water removal shortens collagen and generates large tensile stress; a quantified passive, water-driven actuation mechanism (hygromorph principle). Osmotic stress in tissue is also loosely relevant to tissue-shape work.
works.quote: The consequence is a shortening of the molecule that translates into tensile stresses in the range of several to almost 100 MPa, largely surpassing those of about 0.3 MPa generated by contractile muscles.

works.title: Predictive modelling-based design and experiments for synthesis and spinning of bioinspired silk fibres
works.why: Model-predicted, then synthesised and spun silk fibres; states design rules (block ratio, chain length) and a proportionality between network conductance and modulus. A compose-predict-test template.
works.quote: We find that intermediate hydrophobic/hydrophilic block ratios observed in natural spider silks and longer chain lengths lead to outstanding silk fibre formation.

works.title: Large Deformation Mechanisms, Plasticity, and Failure of an Individual Collagen Fibril With Different Mineral Content
works.venue: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research
works.why: Mesoscale model of mineralised collagen fibril; reports an optimum mineral density for toughness-to-density and strength-to-density. A filler-fraction design rule to test in a filled resin.
works.quote: We also found that a mineralized fibril reaches its maximum toughness to density and strength to density ratios for a mineral density of around 30%.

works.title: The Effective Modulus of Random Checkerboard Plates
works.why: Analytical and Monte Carlo treatment of effective modulus of random two-phase checkerboard plates, including percolation effects and specimen-size dependence; applies to voxel-style two-material prints.
works.quote: In small specimens, we find that the onset of percolation causes significant discontinuities in the effective modulus, whereas in large specimens, the influence of percolation is smaller and gradual.

works.title: Mechanics of fragmentation of crocodile skin and other thin films
works.why: States a mechanics law for a surface pattern: polygon size of a cracked thin film is set by fracture energy and Young's modulus, matched to crocodile head skin. A candidate formalisable morphology law and a patterned-coating design rule.
works.quote: We find that the characteristic size of fragmentation, defined by the mean diameter of polygons, is strictly governed by mechanical properties of the film material.

works.title: Biological materials by design
works.why: Topical review of designing engineered materials from building blocks upward with multiscale models linked to synthesis and testing, including wood case studies and engineered fibre composites.
works.quote: Recent developments in this field illustrate a new paradigm by which complex material functionality is achieved through hierarchical structuring in spite of simple material constituents.

works.title: Flaw tolerance promoted by dissipative deformation mechanisms between material building blocks
works.why: States a design rule for flaw-tolerant composites (maximise fracture toughness relative to maximum stored elastic energy), demonstrated with 2D coarse-grained simulations; candidate constraint for eliminating designs.
works.quote: we establish that better flaw tolerance can be achieved by maximizing fracture toughness relative to the maximum elastic energy available in the material

works.title: Materiomics: An ‐omics Approach to Biomaterials Research
works.why: Defines materiomics: combining computational screening of large material-property libraries with experiment to design tailored materials; the framing our constraint-then-screen pipeline sits in.
works.quote: The field of biomaterials research is only beginning to develop and adopt these approaches, an effort which we refer to as "materiomics".

works.title: Modelling the mechanics of partially mineralized collagen fibrils, fibres and tissue
works.venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
works.why: Multiscale model of graded mineralisation at the tendon-to-bone attachment; percolation of the stiff phase controls stiffening, and a compliant zone appears between the two tissues. Directly informs graded joints between dissimilar printed materials.
works.quote: In the five possible sequences of mineralization studied, percolation of the bioapatite phase proved to be an important determinant of the degree of stiffening by bioapatite.

works.title: Mesoscale mechanics of wood cell walls under axial strain
works.why: Coarse-grained wood cell wall model reproducing elastic, plastic and high-strain stiffening regimes and the dependence of modulus on microfibril angle; a fibre-angle design rule for an architected plant-like material.
works.quote: Our model shows that hemicellulose deforms in a stick-slip motion as the fibrils shear, resulting in permanent deformation without causing material damage, and leading to the characteristic softening of wood as deformation is increased.

works.title: Synergetic Material and Structure Optimization Yields Robust Spider Web Anchorages
works.why: Theoretical model plus mesoscale simulation of silk attachment discs: peeling angle self-optimises and hierarchical branching raises delamination force. A stated structural rule for anchorages, of direct interest to an architecture practice.
works.quote: Additional hierarchical branching of the anchorage increases efficiency, where both the delamination force and toughness modulus increase with a splitting of the cross-sectional area.

works.title: Nanoconfinement and the Strength of Biopolymers
works.why: Review of size effects: confining fibrils or mineral platelets at critical length scales governs modulus, strength, extensibility and robustness. Feature-size constraints of this kind bound what a printer resolution can exploit.
works.quote: We outline theoretical and computational analysis as well as experimentation by emphasizing two strategies found in abundant natural materials: confined fibrils as part of fibers and confined mineral platelets that transfer load through a biopolymer interface in nanocomposites.

works.title: Multi-Scale Hierarchical and Topological Design of Structures for Failure Resistance
works.why: Project report: hierarchy and topology designs for damage tolerance, hierarchical Ashby deformation-mechanism design maps, and an aim to make physical test samples of the designed geometries.
works.quote: with disordered heterogeneous distributions of mechanical properties with the potential of uncertainty quantification of fracture properties, and (iv) the development of a hierarchical model that captures deformation mechanisms at multiple hierarchical levels, resulting in hierarchical Ashby deformation mechanism design maps.

works.title: Nonlinear material behaviour of spider silk yields robust webs
works.why: Highly cited (513 in record) paper linking nonlinear silk material behaviour to web robustness; title only, no abstract in record, so the rule itself must be read from the paper.

works.title: Influence of geometry on mechanical properties of bio-inspired silica-based hierarchical materials
works.why: Design rule from simulation: ordered soft/stiff arrangements of a single brittle building block reduce crack-tip stress concentration and can give stable crack propagation.
works.quote: in the strong phase, acts synergistically to reduce the intensity of stress concentrations around a crack tip, and renders the resulting composites less sensitive to the presence of flaws, for certain geometrical configurations it even leads to stable crack propagation.

works.title: Natural stiffening increases flaw tolerance of biological fibers
works.why: Theoretical scaling law plus molecular mechanics: nonlinear stiffening makes fibres flaw tolerant and explains observed fibre sizes.
works.quote: Our findings, established by molecular mechanics and the derivation of a theoretical scaling law, explain experimentally observed fiber sizes in a range of biomaterials and point to the importance of nonlinear stiffening to enhance their fracture properties.

works.title: Universality-Diversity Paradigm: Music, Materiomics, and Category Theory
works.why: Book chapter tying the universality-diversity paradigm to category theory (concepts list category theory, ontology); no abstract in record.

works.title: Thickness of Hydroxyapatite Nanocrystal Controls Mechanical Properties of the Collagen–Hydroxyapatite Interface
works.why: Quantitative geometric rule for a mineral-protein composite: stiffening saturates at a specific platelet thickness; a thickness law for stiff-platelet / soft-matrix composites.
works.quote: The stiffening effect is strongly dependent on the thickness of the mineral crystal until a plateau is reached at 2 nm crystal thickness.

works.title: Reoccurring Patterns in Hierarchical Protein Materials and Music: The Power of Analogies
works.why: Title only: analogy between hierarchical protein materials and music, by the olog authors; second category-theory precedent for cross-domain structural analogies. No abstract in record.

works.title: Flaw Tolerance of Nuclear Intermediate Filament Lamina under Extreme Mechanical Deformation
works.why: Meshwork design rule: a nonlinear stiffening force-extension curve delocalises dissipation and sacrifices single filaments rather than the mesh; transferable in principle to a flaw-tolerant lattice.
works.quote: Here we uncover the physical basis of the material design of nuclear lamina that enables it to withstand extreme mechanical deformation of >100% strain despite the presence of structural defects.

works.title: Bond energy effects on strength, cooperativity and robustness of molecular structures
works.why: General rule relating bond energy to cooperativity and robustness: clusters of weak bonds are robust, strong bonds are strong but not robust; a formalisable trade-off.
works.quote: The cooperative effect of bonding results in an enhanced robustness since the drop of strength owing to the loss of a bond in a larger cluster only results in a marginal reduction of the strength.

works.title: Hierarchical Structure and Nanomechanics of Collagen Microfibrils from the Atomistic Scale Up
works.why: Model validated against experiment giving collagen microfibril moduli (wet, dry, small and large strain) and showing the microfibril is softer than a single molecule; a property anchor.
works.quote: hydrated (wet) collagen microfibrils feature a Young's modulus of ≈300 MPa at small, and ≈1.2 GPa at larger deformation in excess of 10% strain, which is in excellent agreement with experimental data

works.title: Molecular and Nanostructural Mechanisms of Deformation, Strength and Toughness of Spider Silk Fibrils
works.why: Mesoscale silk model: stiff nanocrystals in an extensible matrix, with strength set by crystal size; a two-phase design template (stiff inclusions in a soft matrix).
works.quote: the ultimate tensile strength of silk is controlled by the strength of beta-sheet nanocrystals, which is directly related to their size, where small beta-sheet nanocrystals are crucial to reach outstanding levels of strength and toughness

works.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the α -Helix to β -Sheet Transition in Coiled Protein Filaments: Evidence for a Critical Filament Length Scale
works.why: States a critical filament length separating sliding from a stiffening structural transition; another explicit length-scale threshold law.
works.quote: short proteins with less than 26 amino acids or 3.8 nm length reveal interprotein sliding

works.title: Mechanomutable properties of a PAA/PAH polyelectrolyte complex: rate dependence and ionization effects on tunable adhesion strength
works.why: Stimulus-responsive ('mechanomutable') polymer complex whose adhesion strength shifts with pH, compared against AFM experiments; precedent for a material whose mechanics respond to a chemical signal (track 1 link is by analogy to a shifted response curve, not a gene circuit).
works.quote: The ultimate strength of adhesion for the aligned polymers is shown to range from approximately 15 nN to 40 nN for an equivalent pH range of pH 2.5 to pH 10.

works.title: Materiomics: biological protein materials, from nano to macro
works.why: Defines materiomics as merging material and structure across scales, covering protein, nacre and cellulose / wood systems; the conceptual frame the biomaterial track would cite.
works.quote: An important trait of these materials is that they display distinctive hierarchical structures across multiple scales, where molecular details are exhibited in macroscale mechanical responses.

works.title: Hierarchical simulations for the design of supertough nanofibers inspired by spider silk
works.why: Hierarchical fibre-bundle model predicts strength and toughness of a composite from constituent properties, fractions and arrangement; yields a minimum plastic-phase fraction rule. Reusable as a constraint for a two-phase printed composite.
works.quote: Due to the crack-opening control nature of the simulations, it is also possible to derive a critical minimal percentage of plastic component needed to avoid catastrophic behavior of the material.

works.title: ATOMISTICALLY-INFORMED MESOSCALE MODEL OF DEFORMATION AND FAILURE OF BIOINSPIRED HIERARCHICAL SILICA NANOCOMPOSITES
works.why: Two-level hierarchy in a single brittle material recovers stiffness while raising toughness, with numbers; a geometry-only design rule that maps onto a brittle printable resin.
works.quote: we find a large improvement (≈4.4 times) in toughness over bulk silica, while retaining the high stiffness (to 70%) of the material.

works.title: Nanomechanics of biologically inspired helical silica nanostructures
works.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part N Journal of Nanoengineering and Nanosystems
works.why: Geometry alone (helical form) turns a brittle material ductile with no added component; direct precedent for a morphology-constrained design in one print material.
works.quote: It is found that introducing a helical nanostructural geometry gives the typically brittle silica a highly ductile, yet softer, mechanical behaviour: extensions of 100 per cent to roughly 300 per cent are observed for varying helical geometries.

works.title: Merger of structure and material in nacre and bone – Perspectives on de novo biomimetic materials
works.why: Title only (no abstract in record): highly cited review on nacre and bone as merged structure-material systems and de novo biomimetic materials; core background for a nacre- or bone-like printed composite.

works.title: Alpha-Helical Protein Networks Are Self-Protective and Flaw-Tolerant
works.why: Flaw-tolerance mechanism for a network: failure strain insensitive to flaws via blunting of the crack shape; a design rule a lattice-like printed network could test.
works.quote: We show that the key for these self protecting properties is a geometric transformation of the crack shape that significantly reduces the stress concentration at corners.

works.title: Alpha-helical protein domains unify strength and robustness through hierarchical nanostructures
works.why: Hierarchical Bell model: an analytical structure-property relation for strength versus hierarchical arrangement at constant material use, validated against simulation. A closed-form law of the kind that could be formalised.
works.quote: An optimal combination of redundancies at different hierarchical levels enables superior mechanical performance without additional material use.

works.title: Defining Nascent Bone by the Molecular Nanomechanics of Mineralized Collagen Fibrils
works.venue: ASME International Mechanical Engineering Congress and Exposition (IMECE)
works.why: States a design rule: staggered assembly at a specific optimal molecular length gives toughness; hierarchy combines strength and robustness. Candidate for a formal length-scale constraint.
works.quote: This is achieved by arranging tropocollagen molecules into a staggered assembly at a specific optimal molecular length scale.

works.title: Elasticity and Strength of Beta-Sheet Protein Materials: Geometric Confinement and Size Effects
works.why: Fracture-mechanics strength bound for H-bonded domains and cluster-size rule; a closed-form limit suited to formalisation as an elimination law.
works.quote: Our analysis predicts that individual protein domains stabilized only by hydrogen bonds cannot exhibit rupture forces larger than 100–300 pN in the asymptotic quasi-static limit.

works.title: Asymptotic Strength Limit of Hydrogen-Bond Assemblies in Proteins at Vanishing Pulling Rates
works.why: Closed-form asymptotic strength limit for H-bond stabilised domains; a numeric bound usable as a formal constraint.
works.quote: Our analysis predicts that individual protein domains stabilized only by hydrogen bonds cannot exhibit rupture forces larger than approximately 200 pN in the asymptotic limit.

works.title: Elasticity, strength and resilience: A comparative study on mechanical signatures of α-Helix, β-sheet and tropocollagen domains
works.why: Maps three building blocks to three distinct mechanical roles (resilience, shear strength, elasticity); a compact motif-to-function table for composing a designed material.
works.quote: AH protein domains provide resilience at large deformation through energy dissipation at low force levels, BS protein domains provide great strength under shear loading, and tropocollagen molecules provide large elasticity for deformation recovery.

works.title: Strength limit of entropic elasticity in beta-sheet protein domains
works.why: Two-parameter model (H-bond energy, persistence length) coupling elasticity and strength; states they cannot be treated separately. Formalisable coupling constraint.
works.quote: We show that a rupture initiation condition characterized by the free energy release rate of H-bonds characterizes the limit of WLC entropic elasticity of beta-sheet protein domains and the onset of rupture.

works.title: A multi-timescale strength model of alpha-helical protein domains
works.why: Constitutive strength model over ten orders of magnitude in timescale from two physical parameters; reusable rate-dependent strength law.
works.quote: Here we report a constitutive model that characterizes the strength of an alpha-helical protein domain subjected to tensile deformation, covering more than ten orders of magnitude in timescales.

works.title: Hierarchical coexistence of universality and diversity controls robustness and multi-functionality in intermediate filament protein networks
works.why: States the universality-diversity paradigm: universal building blocks plus hierarchy as an extra design dimension. Conceptual framework for a typed hierarchy of building blocks in a formal design space.
works.quote: In protein materials, the coexistence of universality and diversity is enabled by utilizing hierarchies, which serve as an additional dimension beyond the 3D or 4D physical space.

works.title: Topology Optimization of Smart Structures Using a Homogenization Approach
works.venue: Journal of Intelligent Material Systems and Structures
works.why: Method we could reuse: homogenization-based topology optimization over a parametric microstructure on a grid, with per-point density of two materials as the design variables. Journal version.
works.quote: A homogenization approach is used to find and use effective material properties for the limiting case of an infinitely small microstructure.

works.title: Numerical homogenization of active material finite‐element cells
works.venue: Communications in Numerical Methods in Engineering
works.why: Homogenization of a parametric periodic unit cell with independent volume fractions of two solids and void; gives continuous, differentiable effective properties as functions of the design parameters. This is the lattice-cell-to-effective-property step an architected printed material needs.
works.quote: We present the homogenization of a parametrically defined periodic microstructure in which it is possible to separately control the volume fractions of conventional material, active material and void.

works.title: Autonomous in-silico inorganic materials discovery via multi-agent physics-aware scientific reasoning
works.why: Multi-agent ideate/plan/execute/critique loop for materials design with blinded-evaluator benchmarking; a reusable template for the biomaterial proposal loop, though the cases are inorganic.
works.quote: Benchmarking against frontier models reveals that SparksMatter consistently achieves higher scores in relevance, novelty, and scientific rigor, with a significant improvement in novelty across multiple real-world design tasks as assessed by a blinded evaluator

works.title: Swarms of large language model agents for protein sequence design with experimental validation
works.why: Swarm of residue-level agents with experimental validation of designed peptides; an example of agent-swarm design closed by a physical test.
